name: Argentina 1986 (World Cup champions, Bilardo)
scopeNote: Argentina at the 1986 FIFA World Cup in Mexico under Carlos Bilardo. Period dates (2 June opener vs South Korea, 29 June final vs West Germany) come from the brief; the final date is confirmed by Bleacher Report/Goal Italia, the opener is not stated by a mined page. Most sources give only the match, not the day, so eventDate is the tournament month 1986-06 unless the match is named (final 1986-06-29). The label is 3-5-2 (Bilardo, Wilson, Bleacher Report), sometimes 3-5-1-1 (Goal Italia); a rigid 5-3-2 or a zonal back line seen on SEO pages is not supported by tier A-B sources. Defence: sweeper (Brown) plus two man-marking stoppers (Ruggeri, Cuciuffo). The 3-5-2 was first used in 1984, which is outside the period and only context.
openQuestions: Dates of the group games, the Uruguay round of 16 (22 June is NOT confirmed), the England quarter-final and the Belgium semi-final are not stated in the mined pages; eventDate for them is 1986-06 or the tournament month, and the brief's 2 June opener is unverified from pages.

Sources disagree on when the back three began: Goal Italia says Brown played libero from the first match and Cuciuffo came in from the Italy game; Wilson (SI) says Bilardo started with a 4-4-2 and only unveiled the full 3-5-2 for the England quarter-final; These Football Times says the back three was adopted for the England game.
Sources disagree on who was the free man: Wilson and These Football Times say Brown was the sweeper with Ruggeri and Cuciuffo as markers; an unmined search snippet lists Ruggeri as libero.
Midfield wording differs: Wilson has Batista as ball-winner with Enrique and Burruchaga; These Football Times has Enrique and Burruchaga supplying Maradona and Valdano.

Pressing and zonal-vs-man detail for Argentina's own defending is thin: only Cuciuffo's marking of Galderisi and Francescoli and the pre-final plan for Matthaus on Maradona are verified. No tier A source (Coaches' Voice) was reached, as the session search budget ran out.

Bilardo's Marca 2006 interview and the 1984 'three defenders, five midfielders and two forwards' quote are given only in English translation by Bleacher Report and SI; the original Spanish was not found.

Search (c) in Spanish, (d) squad-building, a second site: search, and the zonal/man search in Spanish were not run or came back empty because the shared web-search budget ran out; no gap pass was possible.

Bilardo quote dates: statedView[0] and [4] are undated recollections (year given as 1986 only); [1] is attributed to the England quarter-final in June 1986. The Atlético Nacional friendly (before the tournament, month May from memory) is kept unverified as outside the period.

sources.title: The story of José Luis Cuciuffo, the World Cup winner who accidentally shot himself dead
sources.evidence: Bilardo changed tack for the famous 2-1 victory over England in the quarter-finals, the pragmatic coach switching the formation to a back three. Cuciuffo, who had begun the tournament as a right-back, was now playing as the left-sided stopper alongside Óscar Ruggeri, while José Luis Brown operated as a sweeper from a slightly deeper position. Argentina would retain this shape for the remainder of the competition.

sources.evidence: Initially, Bilardo had used a 4-4-2, before switching to deploy Jose Luis Cuciuffo as a man-marker, picking up Giuseppe Calderisi in the second game against Italy. With Jorge Luis Brown operating as a libero, that effectively left Oscar Garre to push forward from left back to join the midfield, with Maradona as an attacking central midfielder. (...)
